definitions.explanation: A narrow wooden veranda attached to the outside of a traditional Japanese house, projecting beyond the eaves and so exposed to rain. Contrasts with the covered, interior-side {縁側|えんがわ}.

examples.english: I sat down on the open veranda.

examples.japanese: {濡|ぬ}れ{縁|えん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{眺|なが}めた→眺める：02132_nagameru⟧。
examples.english: I gazed at the garden from the open veranda.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{民家|みんか}→民家：13217_minka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{濡|ぬ}れ{縁|えん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{涼|すず}み→涼む：03927_suzumu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{茶|ちゃ}→茶：03433_cha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}んだ→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
examples.english: I drank tea while cooling off on the open veranda of the old house.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{濡|ぬ}れる→濡れる：00800_nureru⟧ (to get wet) + ⟦{縁|えん}→縁：02182_en⟧ (veranda; from ⟦{縁側|えんがわ}→縁側：04495_engawa⟧). Named for the fact that, lying outside the eaves, it gets wet when it rains. Often a low wooden bench-like platform that doubles as an outdoor seat.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {濡|ぬ}れ{縁|えん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}る→座る：00757_suwaru⟧: to sit on the open veranda
- {濡|ぬ}れ{縁|えん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{設|もう}ける→設ける：14220_moukeru⟧: to install an exposed veranda

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{縁側|えんがわ}→縁側：04495_engawa⟧: traditional veranda — sheltered by the eaves; the standard inner-side version
- ⟦ベランダ→ベランダ：05072_beranda⟧: balcony — modern, often upper-floor
- ⟦テラス→テラス：28798_terasu⟧: terrace; patio — Western-style outdoor platform
